title: Brain cognition lies on a continuum with conserved pre-neural computation

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Brain cognition lies on a continuum with conserved pre-neural computation

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: Given the deep evolutionary conservation of ion-channel and neurotransmitter mechanisms between developmental and behavioural processes, the cognitive capacities of advanced brains are likely on a continuum with, and evolved from, much simpler computational processes conserved at both the functional and molecular levels.

fields.label: Work
fields.value: The Computational Boundary of a "Self": Developmental Bioelectricity Drives Multicellularity and Scale-Free Cognition

fields.label: Chapter
fields.value: Levin M 2019, The Computational Boundary of a "Self": Developmental Bioelectricity Drives Multicellularity and Scale-Free Cognition › Body Patterning and Cognition: A Common Origin

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: Thus, it is likely that the cognitive capacities of advanced brains lie on a continuum with, and evolve from, much simpler computational processes that are widely conserved at both the functional and mechanism (molecular) levels.

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: Levin M, “The Computational Boundary of a "Self": Developmental Bioelectricity Drives Multicellularity and Scale-Free Cognition”, Frontiers in psychology (2019), doi:10.3389/fpsyg.2019.02688; section “Body Patterning and Cognition: A Common Origin”. Scope: Nervous systems and their pre-neural cellular precursors across the tree of life

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on levin-2019-boundary-06: partially-resolvable, resolvability 0.46

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Large comparative databases can test conservation of mechanisms and selected functional capacities. The broad continuum claim is interpretive, and many rival accounts predict the same molecular homology.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Define a graded set of computational capacities and compare their mechanisms across bacteria, unicellular eukaryotes, non-neural metazoans, and nervous systems, testing phylogenetic continuity and homologous molecular implementation.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Molecular conservation does not by itself establish continuity of cognitive capacity.

Cognition and computation admit competing definitions.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:
data existence: 0.65
data adequacy: 0.38
discriminating power: 0.32
analysis feasibility: 0.52
operationalizability: 0.4

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The molecular premise is a comparative-genomics statement, but the claim's point is that cognition itself lies on a continuum with pre-neural computation. No agreed measurement of that continuum exists, so sequence conservation does not confirm or refute it. The same gene families support a continuum story and a story of reused parts in different computations. The distinguishing claim is not empirically fixed.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Molecular conservation of channels and transmitters can be scored from sequences. A continuum of cognitive capacity needs a scale on which brains and pre-neural cells are ordered, and competing scales reorder the same organisms.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Several operationalizations of cognition give different orderings.

Shared molecules are compatible with discontinuous cognitive mechanisms.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:

operationalizability: 0.28
analysis feasibility: 0.15
data existence: 0.08
discriminating power: 0.12
